summary_up_top.suggest: Add a brief takeaway box at the top summarizing the tension between record farmer payments and the 2,000-crore-litre capacity oversupply.

edits.why: The opening mixes navigation breadcrumbs, site boilerplate, and image metadata before the actual article text, which ruins the mobile reading flow.
edits.how: Strip out the site navigation headers, breadcrumbs, and raw Wikimedia image licensing metadata from the very beginning of the post.

edits.why: At 122 words, this paragraph is too dense to scan comfortably on a smartphone screen.
edits.how: Break the paragraph into two shorter chunks at a natural thematic pause.

edits.why: At 154 words, this paragraph creates a massive wall of text on mobile devices.
edits.how: Split the paragraph into two parts around the midpoint sentence.

edits.why: At 173 words, this paragraph is far too long for a phone layout and risks trapping an auto ad awkwardly.
edits.how: Divide the text into two distinct paragraphs.

edits.why: At 157 words, it contributes to reader fatigue on mobile screens.

edits.how: Break the paragraph into two separate paragraphs.

edits.how: Split after the first sentence that asks “Does the surplus actually hold…”, so the next paragraph focuses on the policy implications.

edits.why: Long paragraph blends analysis of incremental volume with a policy recommendation.
edits.how: Create a break before the clause beginning “Which is exactly why the incremental grain‑ethanol volume…”, separating analysis from recommendation.

edits.why: 158‑word paragraph packs industry reporting and methodological notes together.
